title: Holi and Songkran: spring festivals of colour and water
examples: Why do people throw colours at Holi?
Why do people splash water at Songkran?

explain.say: Imagine a day when everyone in the street is allowed to splash you with colour or water, and you laugh and splash back! Look at the two spring festivals on the board.

draw.text: Holi and Songkran: spring festivals of colour and water

explain.say: On the left is Holi, a Hindu festival in India and Nepal at the full moon in March. People throw bright coloured powder called gulal and spray coloured water. Friends, neighbours, everyone joins in! What colour would you throw?
Look at the next points: the night before Holi, people light a bonfire, remembering an old story of good winning over bad. Holi also welcomes spring and is a time to forgive and make up with friends.

Now look at the right: Songkran, the Thai New Year, from 13 to 15 April, the hottest time of year. People have huge water fights in the streets. Water stands for washing away bad luck. Can you find the gentle side of Songkran?

Yes! People pour a little scented water over the hands of grandparents and elders, to show respect and ask for blessings. Great job! Wow fact: Laos, Myanmar and Cambodia have similar water festivals at the same time.

faq.q: Why do people throw colours at Holi?
faq.a: Holi celebrates spring and the victory of good over bad. Throwing colours is a joyful way to welcome the season, and everyone is equal when covered in colour.

faq.q: Why do people splash water at Songkran?
faq.a: Songkran is the Thai New Year. Water stands for washing away bad luck and making a fresh start, and it cools people down in hot April.
Every year from 13 to 15 April in Thailand. Laos, Myanmar and Cambodia celebrate similar new year water festivals at the same time.
Holi is on the full moon of the Hindu month of Phalguna, usually in March. The bonfire, called Holika Dahan, is lit the night before.

faq.q: How do people show respect at Songkran?
faq.a: In a custom called rod nam dam hua, young people gently pour scented water over the hands of elders and receive their blessings.
asks: What do people do for elders at Songkran?

facts: Songkran, the Thai New Year, is celebrated from 13 to 15 April and was added to UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2023.
Holi falls on the full moon of the Hindu month of Phalguna, usually in March.
